title: Play the Tokens for the Highest Score

concept.title: Buy score with the cheapest tokens; when you cannot afford one, sell score for the most expensive token
body: You start with some **power** and **score 0**, and a bag of tokens, each with a value. Every token may be played **once**, in one of two ways. **Face up:** if your power is at least the value, you lose that much power and gain **1 score**. **Face down:** if your score is at least 1, you gain the value as power and lose **1 score**. Tokens can be played in any order, and you may leave some unplayed. What is the **highest score** you can have at any moment? With power 150 and the tokens `100 200 300 400` the answer is 2.

A face-up play should always use the **cheapest** token, because the score gained is the same (1) whatever the token, and the cheaper it is the more power remains. A face-down play should always use the **most expensive** remaining token, because the score lost is the same (1) and the power gained is the largest. So sort the tokens and keep two ends: the cheapest unplayed token at the left, the most expensive at the right.

body.code:
t.sort()
lo, hi = 0, n - 1
score = best = 0
while lo <= hi:
    if power >= t[lo]:                 # buy score with the cheapest token
        power -= t[lo]; lo += 1
        score += 1
        best = max(best, score)
    elif score > 0:                    # sell one score for the most expensive token
        power += t[hi]; hi -= 1
        score -= 1
    else:
        break                          # no power and no score: nothing more can be played
print(best)

body: Selling score for power is only worth it when it lets us buy more score later, but the algorithm does it only when it is the *only* possible move, and the best score is recorded after every purchase, so a useless sale at the very end never lowers the answer. The sort dominates the work: O(n log n).

statement: You have some power, a score of 0 and `n` tokens. A token can be played once: face up (needs power >= its value; power decreases by the value, score increases by 1) or face down (needs score >= 1; power increases by the value, score decreases by 1). Print the largest score you can have at any moment, if you play the tokens in the best way.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `power`: the number of tokens and your starting power.
The second line has `n` numbers: the values of the tokens.

examples.note: Play 100 face up (score 1, power 50); the score cannot go higher: 1.
Play 100 up (power 100, score 1), play 400 down (power 500, score 0), then 200 and 300 up: score 2.

hints: Face up always with the cheapest token, face down always with the most expensive one.
Record the best score after every face-up play.

explanation: The tokens are sorted. While possible, the cheapest token is played face up (score + 1); otherwise, if the score is positive, the most expensive token is played face down. The best score after every face-up play is the answer.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(1) extra.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, power = map(int, input().split())
t = list(map(int, input().split()))

t.sort()
lo, hi = 0, n - 1
score = best = 0
while lo <= hi:
    if power >= t[lo]:
        power -= t[lo]
        lo += 1
        score += 1
        if score > best:
            best = score
    elif score > 0:
        power += t[hi]
        hi -= 1
        score -= 1
    else:
        break
print(best)
